html:
SMTO-BOOT-0044 — The benchmark doesn't recognize a model name you listed

GUID: dac809c4-078b-4978-836f-dc23083e1775
Slug: boot-benchmark-profile-unknown
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • One or more names after --models aren't models this benchmark knows how to start. It stopped before starting or testing anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check each name after --models: it must be spelled exactly as listed, in lowercase, with names separated by commas. The benchmark matches names letter for letter, so one typo makes it stop.
  2. Find the valid names in the list near the top of src/vllm/benchmark_vllm_models.py (for example qwen3-8b-awq), or use --models all to test the standard set. Only models in that list have a start script the benchmark can launch.
  3. To test a model that isn't in the list, start it yourself and run the benchmark with --no-launch and --base-url followed by its address. In that mode the benchmark doesn't start anything, so any name is accepted as a label.

What success looks like

  • The benchmark prints “=== Benchmarking” followed by each model name you listed.

If it still fails

  • Send the exact command you ran to the person who maintains your model setup. Don't change Model or security settings to get around this; only the names in the command need fixing.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The benchmark's --models list contains a name that is not a key in PROFILES in src/vllm/benchmark_vllm_models.py, so it exited with status 2 before launching anything.

What this means

  • Benchmark profile selection includes names absent from this build's profile registry. Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.

Why this can happen

  • Benchmark profile selection includes names absent from this build's profile registry.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare exact selected names with current --help/profile choices.

How to fix it

  • Use exact, comma-separated keys from PROFILES in src/vllm/benchmark_vllm_models.py (for example qwen3-8b-awq), or --models all for DEFAULT_MODELS; --help does not list profile names. To test a model without a profile, start it separately and use --no-launch --base-url, where model names are only labels.
  • Select an exact supported profile from the benchmark command’s --help output.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Every selected profile exists in the installed benchmark build.

What not to do

  • Do not change unrelated model, execution or trust settings to bypass this failure.

Technical notes

  • Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
